notes:
Profile: CloudLingo Assist is a seed-stage B2B SaaS startup (51-200 engs + product) building an embeddable in-app chat assistant for their web product. Inbound came from a self-serve signup; they converted trial credits and quickly reached out about streaming/p99 latency.

Primary ask: sub-200ms p95 for streaming token delivery in US region for interactive in-app assistant. Goal is to use Redwood hosted API for fast TTV (no infra ops) and to avoid early complexity of Dedicated.

Workload characteristics: short-turn dialogues (avg 40-120 tokens per turn), bursts during product onboarding (200-500 concurrent chats), high sensitivity to first-byte latency and smooth chunked streaming to the client. They use a small context window (4-8 KB) with vector-sourced context per session.

Model/preferences: prefer efficient open models with streaming support and predictable latency. Cost sensitive — pilot budget <$5k. Interested in Redwood’s streaming SDK and prefix caching to reduce tokens. Wants an A/B fallback policy: primary model for latency, secondary smaller model when load spikes.

Security / compliance notes: SMB but must integrate SSO (SAML/Okta) and ingest audit logs into their SIEM. They asked about KMS and message retention controls (14-90 days). Residency not required for pilot.

Quotes / call notes: "We need the chat to feel instant — users drop off when it feels sluggish. If streaming is choppy, we won't deploy." — Head of Product.

Suggested immediate actions (from AE/SE): provision limited-scope streaming test tokens, run 30-min sandbox with 50 concurrent synthetic users, capture real p50/p95/p99 token latencies, share results + a short doc showing fallback routing options. Attach: quickstart + sample client for chunked streaming.
